content: There are various types of assays, each designed for specific purposes, including antigen capture assays, bioassays, competitive protein binding assays, crude oil assays, four-point assays, immunoassays, microbiological assays, stem cell assays, and concentration assays, among others. Molecular Biology Assays In molecular biology, assays are essential tools for research and experimentation. DNA Assays To study the interactions between proteins and DNA, several assays are employed: DNase Footprinting Assay: This technique identifies the specific DNA sequences bound by proteins by detecting regions protected from DNase digestion. Filter Binding Assay: Gel Shift Assay: Also known as electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA), this technique detects protein-DNA interactions by observing shifts in the migration of DNA-protein complexes during gel electrophoresis. RNA Assays Nuclear Run-On Assay: Protein Assays Several assays are used to quantify and analyze proteins: Bicinchoninic Acid (BCA) Assay: Bradford Protein Assay: A dye-binding assay that quantifies protein concentration by measuring the absorbance shift of Coomassie Brilliant Blue dye. Lowry Protein Assay: A biochemical assay that determines protein concentration through a reaction involving copper ions and Folin-Ciocalteu reagent. Secretion Assay: This assay evaluates the secretion of proteins or other molecules from cells. Cytotoxicity Assays To assess the toxic effects of compounds on cells, the following assays are commonly used: MTT Assay: Sulforhodamine B (SRB) Assay: A protein-binding assay that quantifies cell density by staining cellular proteins with SRB dye. Viral Assays Viral Plaque Assay: This method quantifies the number of infectious virus particles in a sample by counting the plaques formed on a cell monolayer. Trofile Assay: This assay determines the tropism of HIV, identifying whether the virus uses the CCR5 or CXCR4 co-receptor for cell entry. Cellular Secretion Assays ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay): This technique detects and quantifies specific cellular secretions, such as antibodies or cytokines. ELISPOT Assay: A related method that determines the number of cells secreting a particular substance. Drug Testing Assays are also used for the detection of illegal drugs in biological samples. Environmental Contaminant Assays Assays are employed to detect environmental contaminants, such as: Lead Coliform bacteria Arsenic Assay Methods for Precious Metals Different methods are used to assay raw materials and finished goods containing precious metals. Raw Precious Metals Silver: Assayed using titration. Gold: Assayed using cupellation. Platinum: Assayed using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). Hallmarking of Precious Metal Items Precious metal items, such as jewelry or art, are often hallmarked to certify their metal content.g., 750 for 18k gold). Historically, the touchstone method was used, but modern techniques like X-ray fluorescence (XRF) are now preferred for their precision. Touchstone Method The touchstone method involves rubbing the item on a special stone, treating it with acids, and comparing the resulting color to reference standards. This method is non-destructive and suitable for valuable items but is not effective for white gold due to minimal color variation. It is accurate to within 2-5 parts per thousand and is ideal for flat, large surfaces. However, it is unsuitable for items with chemical surface treatments or electroplating. Fire Assay (Cupellation) Fire assay, or cupellation, is the most precise but destructive method, with an accuracy of 1 part in 10,000. The process involves melting the sample, separating the alloys, and weighing the constituents. It is primarily used for bullion and gold stocks rather than jewelry or art. This was particularly critical when gold and silver coins were used in daily commerce. While most nations no longer produce gold or silver coins for circulation, many mints still produce bullion coins for collectors and investors. The purity and content of these coins are guaranteed by the issuing mint or government. In the UK, the Trial of the Pyx is a ceremonial procedure to verify the quality of newly minted coins.
